scope: Roadman Cycling contact form and contact API: add invisible bot trapping and a conservative server-side classifier for the synthetic payload pattern currently reaching the inbox.

sections.readerQuestion: Can a genuine visitor still send a sponsorship, partnership, support, press, guest or general enquiry without extra visible friction?
sections.usefulAnswer: Yes. The visible form and confirmation flow are unchanged. A hidden honeypot traps basic form-fill bots, while the server discards only submissions whose name and message both match the observed high-entropy synthetic pattern.
sections.evidence: Focused Vitest coverage replays representative synthetic payloads across every contact subject and verifies that genuine natural-language sponsorship, support, partnership, guest, Unicode-name and short-message submissions are accepted and still invoke every downstream integration.
sections.editorialDecision: Keep the protection invisible to visitors, return the same success response to detected bots, and avoid timing checks or broad keyword rules that could reject fast, autofilled or unusually written genuine enquiries.

claimsAndSources: The classifier is based on the repeated structure observed in recent Roadman contact notifications: generated-looking names paired with 16–32-character mixed-case alphabetic messages. Detection requires both signals, except for the standard hidden honeypot. No claim is made that it catches every possible spam campaign.
examplesAndReasoning: Tests cover current two-word generated names, an older single-token name variant, all allowed subjects and representative genuine messages. The earlier elapsed-time rule was removed because autofill and password managers can enable legitimate submissions in under two seconds.
voiceAndCuts: No public copy was added. The implementation keeps the existing success language and logs only a reason code, never the visitor's personal details.
desktopReview: Codex rendered the changed /contact route locally from commit 0efdbf3 at 1365 × 900. The complete page, contact form and all subjects were visible with no overflow or Next.js error overlay. The honeypot remained outside the viewport. A full-page screenshot was inspected.
mobileReview: Codex rendered the changed /contact route locally from commit 0efdbf3 at 390 × 844. The stacked information cards, every genuine-contact field and the submit button fit without horizontal overflow or an error overlay. The honeypot remained outside the viewport. A full-page screenshot was inspected.
productAndOfferAccuracy: The change affects contact submission handling only. Contact subjects, form labels, response wording and all public product or membership offers remain unchanged.
